Why does a spoon look broken in water?
Why does a spoon look broken in water?
Pull it out,
and it's perfectly straight.
You see the spoon
by the light that leaves
it and reaches your eye.
In water,
light travels about
a quarter slower
than in air.
So a ray leaving
the water at a slant
bends at the surface,
tipping flatter.
But your brain assumes
the ray never bent.
It traces each ray
straight back,
to a spot higher
than the spoon really is.
The part in the air
appears where it is.
The part under water
appears lifted.
So the spoon seems
to snap right
at the surface.
The spoon is not bent.
The light is.
